newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 24.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.

- The Dunnes payments tribunal may suspend its formal sittings next week after hearing evidence from politicians including former transport minister Michael Lowry, prime minister John Bruton and foreign minister Dick Spring.
- The governing coalition will enter an election campaign shortly with a potential bonus seat arising from the unexpected decision by parliamentary chairman Sean Treacey to retire from politics.
- About 25 couples will have to remarry because they did not give enough notice of their intention to wed.
- The Central Bank's currency dilemma eased slightly yesterday as the pound gained a little against a weakening sterling and fell back against the mark.
- A defiant Michael Lowry last night insisted that he would contest the general election despite recent claims at the payments to politicians tribunal.
- The EU last night forecast that Ireland would join the single European currency on time but warned that public spending must be curbed.
- A leading jockey was badly injured at Punchestown yesterday when his horse fell heavily at the final fence in the Heineken Gold Cup.
- Confirmation of 600 new IDA-backed jobs for Dublin and Galway yesterday brings the total number of jobs announced by the industrial development agency this year to 5,800 from 37 separate projects.
- Lawyers for Dunnes Stores are considering suing Charles Haughey for the return of the 1.3 million pounds allegedly given to him by Ben Dunne.
- Pressure from Brussels to squeeze spending in preparation for the European currency leaves the government on a collision course with farmers and healthcare workers.
- The Labour Party last night dismissed suggestions that they had done some sort of deal with parliamentary chairman Sean Treacey to encourage him to retire.
